{{Quote|The term ''Sith'' actually refers to a species of red-skinned beings who were native to Korriban.|[[Vestara Khai]]|<ref name="Ascension">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]''</ref>}}
The '''Sith''', known alternatively as the '''Sith People''', '''Red Sith''', or '''Sith Purebloods''', were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Color/Legends|red]]-skinned [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] that originated on the [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], before eventually resettling on the [[Water/Legends|ice]]-world of [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]]. Also distinct for their [[Bone/Legends|bone]] spurs, facial tentacles, and genetic predispositions toward both left-handedness and the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], the Sith species coalesced into an [[Sith Empire (Pre-Republic)|empire]] ruled first by [[Sith King|kings]] and later by [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lords]]. After the arrival of the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Exiles]] on Korriban in [[6900 BBY]], interbreeding and genetic manipulation altered the Sith species; over the course of several generations the original species became a hybrid race of Sith and Human heritage. Original Sith blood became a symbol of pride among the Sith, with the term "Sith Pureblood" referring to Sith who had a higher than average concentration of Sith blood.

Despite a society dominated by barbarism and infighting, Sith civilization culminated in a [[Golden Age of the Sith|Golden Age]], after which the species was scattered across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. An eponymous dark side [[Sith/Legends|tradition]] took the species' name, one that, despite numerous manifestations over [[Time/Legends|time]], maintained foundations borne of the customs, [[Sith alchemy/Legends|science]] and [[Sith sorcery/Legends|sorcery]] practiced by the ancient Sith species.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Sith_child.png|thumb|left|A Sith youngling]]
The Sith were a proud and violent [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]]<ref name="JvS:TEGttF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> who originated on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] within the [[Horuset system|Horuset]] [[Star system/Legends|system]] in an isolated [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] region called the [[Stygian Caldera]].<ref name="TEA" /> Sith had a larger than average number of individuals with potential to use [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] in their species,<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref> so high in fact that the entire species<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> was considered strongly<ref name="Databank">{{DB|organization|thesith|Sith}}</ref> [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]].<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> The abundant Force-sensitivity resulted from a symbiotic relationship with the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]],<ref name="TotJC">''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]''</ref> where they &mdash; like the other few creatures that inhabited the planet<ref name="TEA" /> &mdash; derived sustenance directly from the dark side of the Force,<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="TotJC" /> and empowered it in turn.<ref name="TotJC" />

Adult Sith characteristically had skin of a crimson hue,<ref name="END:TSD" /><ref name="LTotS:Precipice">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Precipice]]''</ref><ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> although infants of the species appeared a lighter shade of red.<ref name="GAotS:Funeral">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 2]]</ref><ref name="LTotS:Paragon">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon]]''</ref> However, even though typically a dark red,<ref name="CSWE" /> some members of the species retained more pink shades of skin tone in adulthood.<ref name="GAotS">''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith]]''</ref><ref name="FotSE">''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire]]''</ref> Sith had sharp,<ref name="KotOR CG">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> fierce predatory profiles<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> and features all over their bodies,<ref name="KotOR CG" /> including bone spurs protruding from under their skin at various locations<ref name="Crosscurrent">''[[Crosscurrent]]''</ref> like the elbows.<ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" /> Their faces displayed a notable pair of cheek tendrils<ref name="GAotS" /> that hung down from their high cheekbones.<ref name="LTotS:Paragon" /><ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" /> Sith also had cranial horns,<ref name="CSWE" /> pointed teeth, simian mouths below their small noses,<ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" /> and glowing [[Color/Legends|yellow]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /><ref name="KotOR CG" /> covered by cartilaginous<ref name="Crosscurrent" /> eyebrow&ndash;stalks.<ref name="LTotS:Paragon" /><ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" /> In addition, some Sith had long bony chins,<ref name="CSWE" /><ref name="GAotS" /> while others did not show this trait and instead possessed less prominent chins that receded from their mouth.<ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" /><ref name="Legacy">[[Legacy (2006) 30|''Legacy'' (2006) 30]]</ref> Most Sith had three clawed<ref name="LTotS:Ptn">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Pantheon]]''</ref> digits on each hand, and three on each foot; two forward facing and one backward facing.<ref name="GAotS" />However, some Sith had five digits on their hands and feet, such as Sek'nos Rath. The Sith were commonly left handed too, and as a result, their signature weapon, the [[lanvarok]], was constructed only for their left-handed tendencies.<ref name="END:TSD" />

The cheek tendrils on the jowls of Sith that descended from their cheekbones displayed different expressions amongst their species through twitching and other movements.<ref name="LTotS:Paragon" /><ref name="Crosscurrent" /> For example, slight curling of the tendrils showed that the particular Sith was of a rejuvenated attitude, while stroking of the right tendril was an expression of thoughtfulness.<ref name="LTotS:Paragon" /> Also, quivering of the tendrils could show signs of anger, as well as a questioning expression when coupled with raising of the eyebrow&ndash;stalks. The Sith &mdash; specifically the Massassi subspecies &mdash; also had very keen senses relative to those of Humans, particularly their hearing, despite their small ears.<ref name="Crosscurrent" />

===Hybridization===
{{Quote|They figured out a way to mingle their DNA with that of the Sith natives, and gradually that species became extinct.|Vestara Khai, speaking of the Dark Jedi and their Sith subjects|<ref name="Ascension" />}}
[[File:Sith_Empire_percentage.png|thumb|right|180px|More than 98% of [[Tenebrae|Vitiate's]] Sith Empire was of pureblood Sith descent.]]
After their arrival in [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith space]] after the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]] ([[7000 BBY|7000]]—[[6900 BBY|6900]] [['ABY-BBY' dating system/Legends|BBY]]), [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Exiles|Dark Jedi]] began to interbreed with the Sith. For nearly two thousand years, superstition, loyalty and sympathy were bred out as the two groups interbred, and qualities such as cunning, ambition and affinity to the Force were favored, which shaped Sith society over the centuries.<ref name="KotOR CG" /><ref name="Heritage of the Sith">{{InsiderCite|88|Heritage of the Sith}}</ref><ref name="Inhabitants">{{HolonetOld|inhabitants|sith-pureblood|Sith Pureblood}}</ref> In the Sith Empire, as time progressed pure-blooded Sith were steadily bred out,<ref name="END:TSD" /> resulting in only a few pure-blooded Sith left in the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] by the time of the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] (5000 BBY).<ref name="CSWE" /> By [[44 ABY]], the Sith species was believed to have gone extinct due to the interbreeding process.<ref name="Ascension" />

Characteristics shown would be determined depending on how much Dark Jedi or Sith blood an individual possessed due to interbreeding. By the time of the Great Hyperspace War, the majority of the Sith within the Empire displayed mainly Sith traits. It was common for the Sith of this age,<ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" /> especially half&ndash;breeds (like [[Ludo Kressh]]<ref name="CSWE" /> and [[Marka Ragnos]]<ref name="DSS">''[[The Dark Side Sourcebook]]''</ref>) to have four digits on each of their hands.<ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" /> [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]], who had one of the purest Dark Jedi lineages in the Sith Empire, with minimal Sith ancestry,<ref name="TNEGtC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> showed many Human features, including five digits on his hands and feet, as well as the absence of bone spurs and eyebrow-stalks. However, he maintained qualities of the Sith species such as cheek tendrils<ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" /> (albeit shorter than those of purer Sith lineage),<ref name="LTotS:Ptn" /> and red skin.<ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" />

However, some such as the hybrid<ref name="Inhabitants" /><ref name="Daniel Erickson Quote">{{TORweb|url=community/showthread.php?p=2888884#post2888884|text=Playing SWTOR on older computer systems.}}</ref> Sith Purebloods in the [[Great Galactic War]] showed even more dilute Sith characteristics than the likes of Sadow. One such example was [[Exal Kressh]], who only expressed Sith traits such as red skin, glowing yellow eyes, and Force-sensitivity. All other features such as cheek tendrils or eyebrow-ridges were not present,<ref name="BotE">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic, Blood of the Empire]]''</ref> though some other members did show other features shared with the original species.<ref name="Inhabitants" /><ref name="Species Reveal">{{TORweb|url=news/news-article/20100806|text=New Playable Species!|nolive=1}}</ref> Some members even expressed more features than the actual Sith species showed; like the presence of extra pairs of cheek tendrils.<ref name="Inhabitants" /><ref name="Cinematic">{{TORweb|url=info/news/blog/20101231|text=Developer Blogs: Cinematic Design}}</ref> In fact, the Sith Purebloods were thought to be very different from the original Sith species as a whole,<ref name="Daniel Erickson Clarification">{{TORweb|url=community/showthread.php?p=4488768#post4488768|text=Daniel Erickson Clarifies the Position of Purebloods in the Sith Empire|nobackup=1}}</ref> and to be a Pureblood required that one had retained enough traits shared with the original species to be visually clear in their appearance.<ref name="Inhabitants" /> Elderly Purebloods showed signs of old&ndash;age through their skin developing deep wrinkles, paling and mottling with dark brown age spots. Aged Purebloods also tended to have withered tendrils.<ref name="Revan" /> Unlike their ancestors, Sith Purebloods did not exist as an entirely Force-sensitive race, though it was extremely rare to find members unable to manipulate the Force.<ref name="Inhabitants" /><ref name="Daniel Erickson Clarification" />

The extremes of hybridization were shown in an individual named [[Ebya T'dell]], who was part of the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]] around [[4985 BBY]]. Though considered Human, she had unusually pink skin and high cheekbones, which were considered to be signs of apparent Sith species ancestry. Further still, many of the so-called Human crew of the ''[[Omen]]'' in the Lost Tribe had had some degree of interbreeding with the Sith species,<ref name="LTotS:Paragon" /> though they showed no morphology to suggest it<ref name="LTotS:Skyborn">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Skyborn]]''</ref> &mdash; their Force-sensitivity was the only known feature they retained from the interbreeding.<ref name="LTotS:Precipice" /> After [[3000 BBY|2000 years]], deformities seen in the Lost Tribe were associated as being related to the Red Sith originally in the Lost Tribe,<ref name="LTotS:Ptn" /> and even in [[44 ABY]], it was deemed possible for Lost Tribe descendants to still have traces of Sith DNA.<ref name="Ascension" />

By [[3642 BBY]], it was estimated that 97.8 percent of the Sith Empire's population had some amount of Sith ancestry, but the amount was usually insufficient to express itself in any noticeable way.<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>

The certain Dark Jedi traits inherited from the Dark Jedi&ndash;Sith interbreeding Post&ndash;Hundred-Year Darkness were selected for by some individuals,<ref name="GAotS" /> claiming that they were the strongest because of it.<ref name="GAotS:Fabric">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 3]]</ref> However, others were not supporters of this blood over Sith bloodlines;<ref name="DSS" /> some being proud of their Sith traits and lineage,<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> as well as despising any other species<ref name="JATM" /> and their inclusion in the Sith Empire. From the view of the Red Sith, none other than themselves should be considered Sith.<ref name="LTotS:Paragon" />

==Society and culture==
===Culture===
{{Quote|The Sith had strictly defined castes [&hellip;] There was no transitioning from one to the other.|Vestara Khai|<ref name="Ascension" />}}
[[File:RagnosFuneral.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The [[Funeral of Marka Ragnos]].]]
Though they were in an almost constant state of war, their civilization was quite sophisticated; they saw these acts not as cruel or barbaric, but simply basic aspects of existence. They were notable for engaging in supposedly primitive practices such as sentient sacrifices in the name of their gods.<ref name="END:TSD" /> Their constant warring led to a dwindling of the population on their original homeworld of Korriban as well as cultivated an intensely xenophobic society.<ref name="JATM" />

Native Sith culture included the [[Sith (language)|Sith]], the consumption of [[bloodsoup]], a rigid and stratified caste-based society, live sentient sacrifices to the Sith deities and use of ancient and arcane [[Sith alchemy/Legends|alchemy]] and [[Sith sorcery/Legends|sorcery]]. For the Sith, war and violence were just as much a part of the natural order of life as peace or serenity. Their social order was very rigid,<ref name="END:TSD" /> and while many rose to the title of [[Sith King]],<ref name="Book of Sith" /> only the first, King [[Adas]], ever attained the position of overlord. Another aspect of Sith culture, the creation of [[Sith holocron/Legends|Sith holocrons]] to record knowledge, originates from their first contact with the Rakata of the Infinite Empire.<ref name="END:TSD" />

One aspect that originated from Korriban was the position of Shadow Hand; a title that was analogous to that of a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]]. One of the oldest and greatest strengths of the Sith was their knowledge of sorcery. This great power allowed them to accomplish great feats such as causing stars to go supernova.<ref name="KotOR CG" />

===Castes===
[[File:Massassi-JATM.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The priestly Kissai and warrior Massassi castes.]]
{{Quote|In times long past, the Sith race proved malleable&hellip;splitting into a meek and servile slave class&hellip;an intelligent and nimble engineer class&hellip;others interbred with the early exiled Jedi&mdash;like the ancestors of Ludo Kressh&mdash;watering down the powerful bloodlines&hellip;but most useful of all were members of the vicious Massassi Warrior class.|Naga Sadow describes the Sith caste system|<ref name="GAotS:Pawns" />}}
The Sith society was very hierarchical, utilizing both a rigid caste system and a stratified rank structure to put its subjects in their proper place.<ref name="Book of Sith" /> Each caste was sometimes referred to as a subspecies of Sith.<ref name="KotOR CG" /> All Sith castes were red-skinned humanoids with distinctly sharp, predatory features and tentacle beards.<ref name="GAotS:Funeral" /> Among the Sith, the stroking of a right cheek tendril was a sign of thoughtfulness. After interbreeding with the Dark Jedi exiles, the original members of the species became known as '''Red Sith'''.<ref name="LTotS:Precipice" /> Their caste system included the skilled and intelligent Zuguruk caste, the priestly Kissai caste, and the war-like Massassi caste.<ref name="Book of Sith" />

The following were notable castes present amongst the Sith:
*'''[[Zuguruk]] Caste''': The Zuguruk were notably loyal engineers who built and maintained Sith technology, including droids, starships, and tombs.<ref name="Book of Sith" />
*'''[[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] Caste''': Massassi were the warrior caste of the Sith. This was because Massassi tended to be taller and stronger than the other Sith castes, this combined with the natural Sith aggression made very efficient and vicious soldiers for the Sith military. Massassi were not very intelligent but they could be trained well enough to carry out complex battle plans and maintain their equipment, starships, and weaponry making them very useful to the Sith Empire. The Massassi's loyalty had to be earned but once it was they were unswervingly obedient to the Dark Lord of the Sith; they were also loyal to the individual [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] they served, though this loyalty was secondary to their loyalty to the Dark Lord.<ref name="LTotS:Paragon" /><ref name="FotSE" /><ref name="GAotS" /> The Massassi also had a complex language of their own, which may be related to [[Sith (language)|Sith]].<ref name="Word" />
*'''[[Kissai]] Caste''': The Kissai were the priest class in the Sith caste system and were known to study the nature of the Dark side of the Force and practice ancient Sith sorcery and alchemy. The Kissai were just as ruthless as the Massassi, but they were more intelligent, cynical, observant and lacked the physical advantages that Massassi possessed.<ref name="END:TSD" />
*'''[[Slavery/Legends|Slaves]]''': While not a full caste like the others, slaves still occupied an important part of the Sith social order. Sith slaves could be any of a myriad of species ranging from [[Herglic/Legends|Herglic]], [[Human/Legends|Human]], [[Mrlssi]], and their own kind. Slaves were typically referred to by the scornful epithet "[[Grotthu]]."<ref name="Book of Sith" /> The Sith slaves among them were a meek and servile sub-species, the lowliest in Sith hierarchy.<ref name="GAotS:Pawns" /> Pure blooded among them had only three digits on each hand unlike the other sub-species, but after the fusion of bloodlines with the Dark Jedi Exiles, the Slaves seemed to have four digits. They worshiped the Sith Lords as gods, and were often used as sacrifices. The Sith Lords used them for slave labor. When a Sith Lord died, his slaves were buried alive with his body in his tomb on Korriban.<ref name="GAotS:Funeral" />

===Technology===
The Sith art of alchemy allowed them to imbue objects as well as living beings with the dark side.<ref name="JATM" /> Due to their great skill in sorcery, the Sith often created Talismans in order to focus their concentration as well as to further tap great amounts of dark side power. Such artifacts were often used during long elaborate rituals and allowed a sorcerer to temporarily enhance their abilities. These constructs often took many different forms ranging from crystals to [[Sith talisman/Legends|amulets]]. After encountering Jedi attempting to use their talismans for the light side of the Force, the Sith developed ensnarement talismans which, when used, turned their users to the dark side. This in turn led to Sith artifacts being outlawed following the destruction of the Sith. In addition to these artifacts, the Sith long ago developed healing talismans after a revolt led by Naga Sadow which led to pure blooded Sith finding means to provide an advantage to their faction. Healing talismans worked by quickening natural healing processes but at the expense of the user's connection to the Force. Another talisman was the shield talisman that worked by absorbing any form of energy attack and using that as a power source for the relic. Following the destruction of the Sith Empire, the Jedi discovered that talismans were very difficult to destroy due to different means employed in obliterating them - some made use of the destruction of physical components while skilled [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] were sometimes needed to remove the reservoir of Dark side energy in the relics and some were even capable of being destroyed by the dark side only. This led to certain talismans being hidden while others were placed in hazardous locations such as nebulas or stars in order to prevent them from falling into anyone's hands.<ref name="TotJC" />

Talismans were not the only Force empowered artifacts that the Sith were capable of creating. They had long ago learned that the usage of the Force created ripples that could be sensed by others which led to the creation of [[Force mask]]s in order to hide this emanation from others.<ref name="TotJC" /> In addition, they were also capable of creating potent toxins such as [[Sith poison]]s that weakened their targets from the influence of the dark side.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> While there were many forms of common artifacts used by the Sith, there were certain relics that were unique and created by individual Sith Lords. This had led to several specially crafted items such as the [[Gauntlet of Kressh the Younger]], [[Muur Talisman]], [[Dreypa's Oubliette]], [[Eye of Horak-mul]], [[Helm of Dathka Graush]], [[Scepter of Ragnos]], [[Sword of Ieldis]] and the [[Heart of Graush]] as well as the [[Yoke of Seeming]].

During ancient times, the Sith often made use of tomes and manuscripts to record their knowledge. These scrolls and tablets contained teachings on how to learn certain techniques ranging from alchemy to weapon crafting to sorcery. It was only later that the Sith began to adopt holocrons as teachings tools.<ref name="JATM" /> One piece of technology that did not originate from the Sith was [[Sith holocron/Legends|holocrons]] which had been originally adapted from the Rakata.<ref name="KotOR CG" /> Following this event, holocrons became a preferred method of storing Sith teachings, though they were considered rare. By transferring a portion of the user's personality into the device as well as imbuing it with the Force, they were capable of creating a [[Gatekeeper/Legends|Gatekeeper]] that was a sentient presence that interacted with future users. As the different creators of holocrons had different specialities, it meant that these data storage devices often contained aspects of a single field of Sith lore. This had led to the side effect of certain Sith teachings being lost because the knowledge was either never recorded or destroyed. Those holocrons that had survived over the years either fell into the hands of dark side acolytes or remained within the sanctuaries of the dead Sith Lords.<ref name="TotJC" /> Their usage also had a corrupting influence on those that accessed its forbidden knowledge.<ref name="JATM" /> While holocrons were used, manuscripts and other means of containing Sith teachings were also used. Such relics included the [[Epistle of Marka Ragnos]] and the [[Codex of Karness Muur]].

Sith alchemy was also regularly used in the creation of weapons such as [[Sith sword]]s. These blades were one of the earliest weapons made by the Sith and were remarkably effective.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> Such blades were treated so that they were reinforced to withstand any blow, which allowed them to combat lightsabers. Their unique creation also meant that they were capable of surviving for thousands of years and in perfect condition.<ref name="TotJC" /> The ancient Sith Lords of Ziost were known to have made use of [[Cortosis-weave]] to create [[Sith Tremor Sword]]s: a powerful [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblade]] melee weapon. In addition, they made use of Sith alchemy to enhance the strength as well as destructive power of blade weapons such as [[Sith war sword]]s.<ref name="KotOR CG" /> A primitive ranged weapon created by the Sith was the [[Lanvarok]] that was originally used as a hunting tool. In contrast to weapons, the Sith also crafted dark armor which provided additional protection for their wearers and were crafted to meet the individual requirements of their user.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" />

[[File:NagaSadow2.jpg|thumb|right|130px|The Sith Lord Naga Sadow using his Meditation Sphere.]]
This talent in Sith alchemy also extended to create biological weapons which allowed them to genetically engineer creatures to become tainted abominations. Such feats were used to engineer the [[Tuk'ata/Legends|Tuk'ata]] that served as guardians for various Sith tombs. In fact, the ancient Sith Empire made use of this art to create [[Chrysalide|Chrysalis beasts]] that were used as guards as well as pets to various Sith Lords. They even engineered weapons to be employed for sieges such as mutating [[Silooth/Legends|Silooth]] in order to break enemy defenses.<ref name="JATM" />

Sith were noted for considering the construction of structures and edifices to be a work of art. They felt that such buildings were an extension of their creators personality. This had the resulting effect of preventing enemies from being able to properly chart the internal structure of such sanctuaries and provided the Sith a tactical advantage.<ref name="TotJC" /> Such techniques were also used to create [[focusing chamber]]s designed to amplify a Sith Lord's power. This allowed the Sith to create vessels such as the [[Sith Meditation Sphere]] that were imparted with a level of sentience as well as the capacity to magnify Force power to great levels. Grander scales of their technological abilities included the creation of Force-empowered superweapons such as the Dark Reaper that was constructed during the years of the Great Hyperspace War.<ref name="KotOR CG" />

==History==
===Early civilization===
[[File:Korriban-TOR.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Korriban, ancient homeworld of the Sith.]]
Sith civilization evolved on the planet Korriban,<ref name="END:TSD" /><ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /><ref name="CSWE" /> leading barbaric<ref name="END:TSD" /><ref name="Revan" /> and hedonistic lifestyles while<ref name="Revan" /> using the dark side of the Force.<ref name="CSWE" /> The Sith had a natural symbiotic relationship fused with the dark side.<ref name="TotJC" /><ref name="Inhabitants" /> They fed on it and empowered it, developed and perfected techniques of the dark side through it, that were once thought impossible&mdash;such as [[Sith sorcery/Legends|sorcery]]. Though they had great power, the Sith were not united, and lived in tribal "[[Circle (Sith Pureblood)|circles]]," led by one or more Sith sorcerers who were responsible for the safety and protection of their people.<ref name="TotJC" /> The state of war between the Sith nations on Korriban was common in their society, but this existence was treated as one on par with peace and serenity by the Sith people. They did not, or could not differentiate one state from another, and this, including other barbaric practices, were accepted into Sith society not as being antagonistic or contrary, but integral to their lives. They could not see these barbaric practices they undertook as anything else but their only way to live; their ultimate existence. Sith civilization described as such was said to have began around the year [[100,000 BBY/Legends|100,000 BBY]];<ref name="END:TSD" /> however, the [[Dark Holocron]] contained Sith lore and forgotten histories that dated back even further.<ref name="EotW">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 1]]</ref> As recorded by ''[[Jen'jidai]]'' [[Sorzus Syn]] in [[Sorzus Syn's chronicle|her 6900 BBY chronicle]], the monuments in the [[Valley of Golg]] stood long before the advent of the [[Zhell/Legends|Zhell]] civilization on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]<ref name="Book of Sith" /> around [[200,000 BBY]].<ref name="Valley of Golg">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-2-ancient-coruscant|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 2 - Ancient Coruscant}} establishes that the [[Zhell–Taung war|war]] between the [[Battalions of Zhell]] and the [[Taung/Legends|Taungs]], which included the battle at [[Great Zhell]], occurred approximately 200,000 [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior to [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]] and lasted for several [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]]. [[Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 35|''Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection'' 35]] further places the war in [[200,000 BBY]]. ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]'' (p. 27) establishes that the Valley of Golg stood long before the civilization of Zhell existed on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] which would place the construction of the valley at some point long before around 200,000 BBY.</ref>

It was speculated among some historians that several of the ancient Sith practices, such as the consumption of [[bloodsoup]], were due to an interaction been Sith and [[Anzat (species)|Anzati]] cultures at some point in pre-history. The [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Volfe Karkko]] was fond of remarking to the Jedi Knights that the Anzati&mdash;his own species&mdash;"''remember the very first Sith''" after studying a [[Sith holocron/Legends|Sith holocron]]. However, beyond his claims, there is no further evidence to support this theory.<ref name="END:TSD" />

During this time Sith recorded information in scrolls, tomes and tablets. These contained dark knowledge, such as writings that described dark side [[Force power/Legends|powers]], [[Sith alchemy/Legends|alchemy]], the construction of Sith weapons and artifacts, and treatises on the domination and destruction of others. However many of these ancient writings were imbued with the madness of those Sith who wrote them, and consequently, the knowledge was capable of driving unprepared seekers of knowledge to insanity.<ref name="JATM" /> It was known that the Sith already had a great knowledge of the depths of their powers by this era, specifically the rage and revenge that lead to the dark side of the Force. Demonstrating this, the Sith drove off an [[Incursion of Korriban|incursion]] by the [[Killik/Legends|Killiks]] around [[30,000 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:SeknosRath-ForceStorm1.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Sek'nos Rath]], an example of a Sith Je'daii around 25,793 BBY.]]
Around [[36,453 BBY]] [[Tho Yor]] pyramid ships gathered the galaxy's best Force-sensitive philosophers, priests, scientists and warriors from around the galaxy to the Force-strong world of [[Tython/Legends|Tython]]. Some members of the Sith species were taken from their Korriban homeworld in this time, to eventually become some of the first [[Je'daii Order|Je'daii]]. After [[25,793 BBY|ten millennia]] of studying a balance between what would be called the light and dark sides of the Force, descendants of these founders still existed as Je'daii Masters, Journeyers and diplomats in the Tython system. Shortly before the outbreak of the [[Force Wars]], an event caused the light and dark side of the Force to polarize within the minds of the Je'daii, eventually culminating with the formation of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="Comic Book Resources">{{WebCite|url=https://www.cbr.com/nycc-exclusive-ostrander-and-duursema-unveil-star-wars-dawn-of-the-jedi|text=NYCC EXCLUSIVE: Ostrander and Duursema Unveil "Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi"|archivedate=20200817183352|author=Shaun Manning|date=2011-10-13}}</ref>

===''Sith'ari''===
====Unification====
[[File:SithKingAdas-BoSSFtDS.png|thumb|left|200px|Sith King Adas, the Sith'ari of ancient Sith.]]
Civil war between Sith nations on Korriban continued for many thousands of years, but eventually, Korriban was united under the rule of a single Sith&mdash;[[Adas]]. Adas was raised as a chosen being due to the unusual nature of his charcoal colored skin, and he grew into a powerful being, demonstrating great skill in fighting as well as great intelligence. Adas also had an extreme talent for [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith sorcery]]. Forging his own massive battle axe through the use of Sith alchemy, Adas led the unification of Korriban's warring nations.<ref name="END:TSD" />

Though with much bloodshed, Adas united the disparate nations of Korriban into a single kingdom, becoming an inflexible and undisputed leader of the Sith around [[28,000 BBY]].<ref name="END:TSD" /><ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /><ref name="KotOR CG" /> Adas became the Sith King and God of the Sith as his reign continued and he earned the title of ''[[Sith'ari/Legends|Sith'ari]]'', meaning "overlord"<ref name="END:TSD" />&mdash;the perfect being.<ref name="KotOR CG" /> Eventually, his people came to believe that his reign would be eternal, and that Adas was immortal.<ref name="END:TSD" />

Adas had been ruling [[27,700 BBY|three hundred years]]<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> when the dark sided invaders of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] arrived on Korriban.<ref name="END:TSD" /> The Rakatans hid their ultimate agenda from Adas, and tried to lull him into their confidence by teaching the Sith new technologies such as how to build and store knowledge inside a device known as a [[Holocron/Legends|Holocron]]. Eventually however, the Rakatan's tried to conquer the Sith people, and the ''Sith'ari'' rose to repel the invaders with the indomitable will of his people behind him.<ref name="END:TSD" /> During this time of war, it was known that the Rakata also took at least one prisoner—[[Raspir]], who was once a court [[Sith sorcerer|sorcerer]] of King Adas, but was imprisoned inside a Rakatan mind trap.<ref name="TUR">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref> Adas took his battle axe to the invaders and managed to outsmart the immensely powerful Infinite Empire despite the advanced technology the Sith were up against, eventually defeating the conquerors.<ref name="END:TSD" /><ref name="KotOR CG" /> From there, he took control of the Rakatan hyperspace-capable craft and spread his rule and Sith civilization to neighboring worlds, including nearby [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]].<ref name="TEA" /> However, in order to secure freedom for his people, Adas was forced to sacrifice his life to guarantee total victory for the Sith.<ref name="END:TSD" /><ref name="KotOR CG" />

====Disintegration====
With Adas's [[Death/Legends|death]], and the absence of his unifying influence, the Sith once again plunged into the previous state of [[Korriban civil war|war]], where reigning combatants arrogantly proclaimed themselves as the new ''Sith'ari''. Over time, the title of Sith Lord as it was translated became relatively common amongst the Sith.<ref name="END:TSD" /> With Korriban devastated by the Rakata,<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> and the constant war all over the planet, the Sith were forced to relocate the Sith capitol to Ziost using new Rakatan Force-based technology the Sith had obtained.<ref name="END:TSD" /><ref name="KotOR CG" /><ref name="TEA" /> There, the priestly Kissai caste oversaw the rebuilding efforts.<ref name="KotOR CG" /> The Sith prospered, continuing to expand their Empire to nearby planets like [[Jaguada/Legends|Jaguada]], as well as to planets further out such as [[Malachor V]] and [[Arbra/Legends|Arbra]].<ref name="Word" /><ref name="KotOR CG" /> But the Rakatans' did more than just give the Sith new technology: they gave the Sith the concept of the dark side of the Force, which conflicted with the Siths' spiritually serene lives of warring, sentient sacrifice to their gods and sortilege.<ref name="Karnak Tetsu">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/KOTORweben5|text=KOTOR Campaign Guide Web Enhancement 5: Karnak Tetsu, Sorcerer of Tund}}</ref>

However, some Sith priests interpreted the death of their ''Sith'ari'', the death of Adas as a sign to reject the Sith concept of life. Declared as heretics, they were banished, and found their way through the Force<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="Karnak Tetsu" /> to the world of [[Tund/Legends|Tund]] using Rakatan [[Force-drive|hyperdrive technology]],<ref name="KotOR CG" /><ref name="TEA" /> and formed a pure-blooded society of Sith sorcerers, based on their new beliefs. The sorcerers lived what they viewed as perfectly harmonious lives, and practiced sorcery, ontology and science, through the Force. They&mdash;like the Rakatans&mdash;believed that all sentients were Force-sensitive, as well as claimed that the omnipresence of the Force proved that the division of the Force (or what they called "the Unity") into true opposites was a falsity.<ref name="Karnak Tetsu" /> It was at this time that recorded history began for the Sith.<ref name="TEA" />

Eventually, the Sith largely abandoned the planet Korriban and it became a ceremonial tombworld, however populations still remained in the form of religious cultists.<ref name="KotOR CG" /><ref name="TEA" /> Over the thousands of bloody years, the [[Sith Empire (Pre-Republic)|Sith Empire]] filled valleys across Korriban with the tombs of the Sith, making them even larger and more impressive as the years went by.<ref name="K:PotLS">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20031002korriban1|series=Korriban: Planet of Lost Souls|text=Part 1: Haunted Hideout}}</ref> These vast cemeteries contained hundreds of tombs belonging to Sith Lords or other powerful dark side users that were built both on and hidden underneath the surface of Korriban.<ref name="JATM" /> One of these valleys was known as the [[Valley of Golg]], an example of the many "Valleys of the Sith Lords" that covered the planet at this time.<ref name="K:PotLS" />

The Sith continued to expand their Empire, encompassing worlds like [[Krayiss II]]; building a Sith [[library-temple]] there by [[14,000 BBY]], where Sith sorcerers would come to meditate and reflect on their experiments&mdash;evolving Sith techniques and manipulation of the dark side.<ref name="A Tale from the dark side">{{WEGCite|story=A Tale from the Dark Side|book=Tales of the Jedi Companion}}</ref> As far back as [[8000 BBY|8000 years before the battle of Yavin]], [[Human/Legends|Humans]] and other [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] species fled during the Tapani Dynastic Era and found their way into Sith space where they interacted with the Sith, though due to the properties of the Stygian Caldera which made hyperspace navigation extremely difficult there, the Sith Empire was largely kept secluded from the rest of the galaxy.<ref name="TEA" />

Over [[7000 BBY|7000 years before the battle of Yavin]], one Sith conqueror known as [[Dathka Graush/Legends|Dathka Graush]] and his forces initiated and won [[Korriban civil war (Dathka Graush)|one]] of the cyclical wars on Korriban,<ref name="K:PotLS" /> leaving most the planet's cities devastated.<ref name="TEA" /> Graush continued to rule on Korriban for [[6950 BBY|50 years]], a rule characterized by his cruelty and the terror he brought to the Sith people on Korriban&mdash;even by Sith standards. Graush was eventually assassinated and entombed in the Valley of Golg. At the point of his death,<ref name="K:PotLS" /> the King of the Sith<ref name="SOM">''[[Luke Skywalker and the Shadows of Mindor]]''</ref> had been in control of two-thirds of Korriban.<ref name="K:PotLS" />

===''Jen'ari''===
====Exile====
{{Main|Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends}}
[[File:Exodus2.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The primitive Sith of Korriban witness the arrival of the [[exiles]].]]
In Republic space, [[7003 BBY|around this same time]] some of the more ambitious [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] in the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Order]] opened themselves up to the dark side of the Force. They experimented with it, and found they could use it to literally bend life itself, able to transform and mutate creatures to their will.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> These "fallen" or "dark" Jedi, as they were known, had previously conducted their dark studies in secret, and were persecuted for their beliefs and defying the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]]. But these Dark Jedi soon emerged in greater numbers, and declared themselves free of the will of the Jedi Council, starting the [[Second Great Schism]].<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /><ref name="Heritage of the Sith" /> Three years later, they rebelled against the Jedi Order as a whole, and a [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|war]] erupted between them. The Jedi constantly battled against these Dark Jedi, forbidding their experiments and practice of their dark side knowledge. While at the same time the Dark Jedi continued to convert Jedi to their cause.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" />

The war between the Jedi and the Dark Jedi continued for one hundred years, and was finally ended at the [[Battle of Corbos]], where the Jedi, who were more numerous,<ref name="Heritage of the Sith" /> overwhelmed the Dark Jedi, and forced the survivors to surrender.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> Unwilling to execute their prisoners, the Jedi chose to purge their names and all evidence of their existence from galactic records, removing them symbolically.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /><ref name="Heritage of the Sith" /> The Jedi then herded them onto a [[Dark Jedi galleon|drone ship]] with no weapons or navigational devices, and banished them into a previously unexplored region of the Outer Rim, far beyond the boundaries of the Republic.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> Their defenseless ship drifted through hyperspace, guided by the dark side of the Force, and finally emerged upon the planet Korriban.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /><ref name="Heritage of the Sith" />

====Conquest====
[[File:Red_Armored_Dark_Lord.jpg|thumb|right|300px|An unnamed [[Unidentified red-armored Sith Lord|Red-armored Sith Lord]] is worshiped by a Sith individual.]]
On Korriban, the Dark Jedi were astonished to find the native Sith as a Force-sensitive people.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> As had been the case since the beginning of Sith civilization, the Sith at this time preferred to remain in a societal structure made up of bands of Sith called tribal "circles", each lead by one or more ruling sorcerers.<ref name="TotJC" /> On [[Discovery of Korriban|arrival]] the primitive,<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> religious,<ref name="TEA" /> superstitious, and barely civilized Sith there greeted the outsiders with their Sith swords, and attempted to terrify the Dark Jedi with crude and imaginative, though impressive illusions using their Sith sorcery.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> However, the Dark Jedi were surprised by the relatively primitive species's dark knowledge&mdash;some of which themselves and the Jedi had never come across&mdash;<ref name="Inhabitants" /> and took particular interest in their various techniques of drawing power from the dark side, seeking to learn it from them.<ref name="TotJC" /> To do this the Dark Jedi went about trying to subjugate the Sith people under their rule, to take the knowledge from them.<ref name="Inhabitants" /> Protective of their secrets, the Sith felt they should prevent the outsiders from obtaining their dark side knowledge,<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> and struck back at the Dark Jedi,<ref name="Inhabitants" /> trying to prove themselves, and drive the Dark Jedi away. But the Dark Jedi eventually proved to be more intelligent and stronger than even the greatest sorcerers of these primitive Sith,<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> and with their Force abilities, lightsabers, and superior technology,<ref name="END:TSD" /> they continued to persist. Ultimately, the Dark Jedi outmatched the natives through their Jedi training and technology,<ref name="Inhabitants" /> and stole the Sith people's knowledge of sorcery and then used it against them.<ref name="TotJC" /> Though, even when defeated the Sith demonstrated honor,<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> the natives eventually became the unwilling subjects of the Dark Jedi.<ref name="TotJC" /> The ''Jen'jidai''&mdash;as they were known in the Sith language&mdash;then used the help of the [[Hakagram Graush|reigning Sith King's]] [[Hakagram Graush's Shadow Hand|Shadow Hand]] to lure the Sith King into their confidence, and destroyed him. Astonished, the Sith never anticipated the sequence of events that lead to the downfall of their King,<ref name="END:TSD" /> and readily accepted the Dark Jedi exiles as their masters,<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> bestowing upon them King Adas's Holocron. The Dark Jedi declared themselves living gods and kings over the Sith people,<ref name="Heritage of the Sith" /> becoming overlords themselves,<ref name="Inhabitants" /> and [[Ajunta Pall]]&mdash;who had personally slew a dozen Jedi at the mining world of Corbos<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" />&mdash;was first to earn the title of ''Jen'ari'', or [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]].<ref name="KotOR CG" />

[[File:XoxaanMuur.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The exiles eventually come to be worshipped as [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lords]].]]
The Sith took to worshiping and devoting their lives to their new masters, who honed their battle arts with new Sith knowledge and expanded their reach from Korriban to neighboring worlds and star systems. Eventually, all of the Sith in previous Sith Empire space were brought under the rule of the Dark Lord of the Sith.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> Ziost was taken as the capital world, where the Dark Lord would reign from,<ref name="Book of Sith" /> and fortresses were built there with towering spires, from which the newly-proclaimed Sith Lords ruled. New [[Starship/Legends|starship]] and weapons were constructed, and with their new knowledge of Sith alchemy, new creatures were produced. The influence of the Dark Jedi on the Sith peoples even managed to benefit the already awe-inspiring Sith architecture.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> The new Sith Lords felt the Sith culture suited their philosophy well,<ref name="Inhabitants" /> and under the rule of the Dark Lord of the Sith, the crude, rigid and highly stratified Sith caste system remained in place, based off the Sith's many subspecies.<ref name="END:TSD" /><ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> Particular interest was given to the Massassi warrior caste, which the Sith Lords used as foot soldiers for their new developing Empire.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> Armed with their new Massassi warriors, weapons, and sorcery, a number of ambitious Sith Lords sought revenge against the Republic. Analyzing the navigational computer from the ship that had brought them to Sith space, these vengeful Sith reprogrammed it for a trip back to the Republic, against Ajunta Pall's wishes.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /><ref name="KotOR CG" /> These Sith Lords and their new armies were not heard of again in Sith space, and failed in their attempt to conquer the Republic, only succeeding in revealing to the Jedi that the Dark Jedi exiles had survived in an unknown region called Sith space, and had took to calling themselves Sith after the people they ruled.<ref name="END:TSD" /><ref name="JvS:TEGttF" />

The Sith Lords that did not go back to the Republic found that other than being able to produce new creatures through Sith alchemy, they were able to produce offspring with the Sith people via alchemical means<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /><ref name="KotOR CG" />&mdash;starting with the Massassi subspecies.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> So, these remaining Lords mingled their Jedi blood with the Sith people, and for almost two-thousand years this process continued, with characteristics such as superstition, loyalty, and sympathy being bred out.<ref name="KotOR CG" /> In contrast, qualities such as ambition, cunning, and raw power in the Force were encouraged throughout the generations.<ref name="KotOR CG" /><ref name="Inhabitants" /> Soon the elite, ruling Kissai class in the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] was almost entirely made up of ruthless, ambitious, and powerful hybridized offspring of the high Kissai priests and the Dark Jedi.<ref name="Inhabitants" />

As time progressed, the magocratic Sith Empire, led by a [[Sith Council|council of Sith Lords]] and a single ruling Dark Lord,<ref name="TEA" /> rapidly expanded their territory,<ref name="Heritage of the Sith" /> sprawling across entire sectors of the galaxy,<ref name="Word" /> though they largely remained in the Stygian Caldera.<ref name="TEA" /> As they expanded, the Sith came into contact with many planets, and as a result, [[Myke]], [[Arkanian/Legends|Arkanian]], and [[Kruskan]] cultures all show hints of Sith influence.<ref name="Word" /> They even came across Tund, where Sith-Human hybrids settled alongside the pure-blooded Sith sorcerers that had found their way there millennia before. By the end of the Empire's expansion they encompassed hundreds of worlds,<ref name="TEA" /> rivaling the Republic,<ref name="Heritage of the Sith" /> from [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]], to [[Ashas Ree/Legends|Ashas Ree]], [[Korriz]], [[Ch'hodos]], and even the distant, early Sith world of [[Malachor V]].<ref name="TEA" /> Each of the ten Sith Council members were also personally in control of a dozen worlds each.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /><ref name="GAotS:Fabric" /> But of all the planets under Sith control, there were only five sacred Sith planets: Ziost, [[Khar Delba]], [[Rhelg/Legends|Rhelg]], Krayiss II, and Korriban.<ref name="TEA" />

Sith society continued to evolve and advanced over this time, discovering new ways to manipulate the dark side of the [[Living Force/Legends|living Force]],<ref name="Heritage of the Sith" /> in their new ordered Empire, ruled by militarism and reverence for the dead. The Sith existed in a state of continual conflict, with Sith Lords raising private armies against their rival Lords, and in their efforts to gain the position of Dark Lord from their reigning ruler. Most inhabitants lived in their ridged, caste determined lives, that still continued to exist after the union of Jedi and Sith blood. Grotthu spent their lives working hard to build tombs for their Lords, and many millions died over the many years in numberless, violent wars within the Empire. Sith Lords were pre-occupied with warring against each other and cowing other civilizations within their range. As a result, not much attention was given to expansion into the Republic, and travel between it and the Empire was extremely rare.<ref name="TEA" /> Those few who did stumble into the Empire were unable to escape due to the Stygian Caldera's unique properties, and soon found themselves as slaves to Sith Lords of minor status. Over generations, the rulers of these immigrants would continually change, and eventually, they would forget where they came from, and called themselves Sith too.<ref name="LTotS:Paragon" /> Being extremely xenophobic,<ref name="JATM" /> the Sith Lords seldom let them rise to any position other than lowly Grotthu under their rule.<ref name="LTotS:Paragon" />

====End of a Golden Age====
At some point from [[5200 BBY]]<ref name="BtM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> to [[5100 BBY/Legends|5100 BBY]],<ref name="5100 date">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 2]] says that Marka Ragnos ruled for a century before 5000 BBY.</ref> the half-breed<ref name="DSS" /> Sith Lord [[Marka Ragnos]] rose to the position of Dark Lord of the Sith<ref name="GAotS:Fabric" /> after a series of short, brutal wars against his adversaries,<ref name="DSS" /> and [[Duel between Marka Ragnos and Simus|defeating]] rival Sith Lord [[Simus]] in combat.<ref name="GAotS:Fabric" /> Ragnos was a very powerful warlord, both physically, and in raw power of the dark side, and as a result he was admired, feared and obeyed as the Sith leader. However, he did have those who contested him, and Ragnos maintained his rule by pitting his enemies against one another, manipulating them into challenging him, or simply assassinating them&mdash;crushing all resistance over the years.<ref name="DSS" /> His century long reign of iron rule resulted in the Empire becoming great, powerful, wealthy, and stable. This was an era which would be known as the [[Golden Age of the Sith]].<ref name="GAotS:Funeral" />

After almost two millennia of interbreeding, the Sith Empire was ruled by what foreign species called the Red Sith, who made up the nucleus, majority, and held power within the Empire.<ref name="LTotS:Precipice" /><ref name="LTotS:Paragon" /> By this stage in the Empire's history, some, though little fully pure-blooded Sith had remained in the Empire,<ref name="CSWE" /> even those of Human ancestry that accidentally found their way into the Empire had at least some degree of mixing.<ref name="LTotS:Precipice" /><ref name="LTotS:Paragon" /> During this time the powerful Sith Lords [[Ludo Kressh]], and his arch-rival [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] rose from their seats on the Sith Council to fight to become the next in line for the position of Dark Lord.<ref name="GAotS:Funeral" /> Like Ragnos, Kressh was a half-breed,<ref name="CSWE" /> and also like Ragnos, he sought to maintain the Empire in its current state of wealth.<ref name="GAotS:Funeral" /> Kressh followed the old traditional ways of the Sith, and was conservative; he believed that the Sith Empire must grow strong within itself before looking to expand into new territories.<ref name="DSS" /> In contrast, Sadow was more of a progressive Sith Lord who claimed to be largely of 'Jedi' blood. He believed that through the Golden Age of the Sith, the Sith Empire had become stagnant and that it was necessary for the Sith to expand and conquer new worlds to bring glory to the Empire, in opposition to Kressh's views.<ref name="GAotS:Funeral" /> Sadow was extremely unusual compared to the other Sith Lords; because of his progressive attitude, those who were not Red Sith were allowed to rise to more prestigious positions under his command.<ref name="LTotS:Paragon" /> This saw Human descended beings becoming miners and captains of ships under Sadow.<ref name="LTotS:Precipice" /> If allowed, those non-Red Sith who excelled in areas such as science and medicine were also able to make breakthroughs in their field, under the very few Lords like Sadow over the millennia, while the Red Sith occupied themselves with the dark side's secrets. The other, vast majority of Sith Lords, notably Kressh, would never allow this to occur, and instead kept the non-Red Sith to lowly slave positions under their command, sticking to the rigid caste system, and feeling that only Red Sith should be allowed positions other than Grotthu.<ref name="LTotS:Paragon" />

[[5000 BBY/Legends|When Ragnos died]] he left a power vacuum in his absence, which Kressh and Sadow immediately stepped up to fill.<ref name="GAotS:Funeral" /> Kressh had the support from most other Sith to become the next Dark Lord, while Sadow controlled the majority of military forces. Potentially, they could have been very powerful together,<ref name="DSS" /> but there could only be one Dark Lord of the Sith. The two fought for the right to rule during Ragnos's funeral. As the battle went on, there was no clear victor, both participants injuring and dominating the other at some point. They were finally interrupted by the spirit of Ragnos himself, who told them about their people's&mdash;the Empire's past, and of the Golden Age of the Sith. He finally disappeared cautioning them to choose their paths wisely. At that moment, a ship carrying the two hyperspace explorers [[Gav Daragon|Gav]] and [[Jori Daragon]] arrived in the Valley of the Dark Lords from the Republic.<ref name="GAotS:Funeral" /> They were instantly seized by the Sith, and put in the prisons of Ziost. Kressh and the Sith Council eventually decided they were to be executed. Sadow however, saw the two Humans as the key to expanding the Sith Empire into the Republic, and secretly rescued the prisoners, killing old Simus in the process to make the event seem like a Republic attack. The Sith Council believed his trickery, and through that, the majority of the Council voted Sadow as the new Dark Lord of the Sith. Kressh was outraged, not accepting Sadow's new status, and declared that he would be the true Dark Lord before [[Ludo Kressh's faction|he and his followers]] stormed out. The Empire was split in two under Kressh and Sadow, igniting a civil war within the Empire.<ref name="GAotS:Fabric" />

Kressh soon discovered Sadow's trickery, and he and his factions launched an [[Battle of Khar Delba|attack]] upon Sadow's [[Naga Sadow's Khar Delba citadel|private fortress]] on Khar Delba.<ref name="GAotS:Pawns" /> Little did he know that it was only a decoy fortress, and once Kressh's forces thought they had destroyed Sadow and all his forces, Sadow's fleet emerged from the dark side of [[Khar Shian]]&mdash;Khar Delba's moon&mdash;where his [[Naga Sadow's Khar Shian citadel|real citadel]] was. In this surprise attack, he caught Kressh's forces off guard and forced Kressh and his remaining followers into a retreat. During this time, Sadow had Jori Daragon fly back to the Republic on the ''[[Starbreaker 12]]'', with Sadow attaching a tracking device to it, giving him a route into the Republic's core.<ref name="GAotS:Flight">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 5|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 5]]</ref>

Sadow then gathered his forces from all over the Empire to Khar Delba, preparing for the invasion of the Republic. However, Kressh's ship appeared above the meeting, and sent down a message to the Sith Lords there, warning them of Sadow's trickery and the doom he thought Sadow would bring to the Empire.<ref name="FotSE:Desparate">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 1]]</ref> In order to block the transmission, Sadow had Gav Daragon activate the automated systems, destroying Kressh's ship in the process, and supposedly killing Kressh along with it. With Kressh thought dead, Sadow now had no one to stop him from invading the Republic, and set about organizing the invasion forces.<ref name="FotSE:Desparate" /><ref name="FotSE:Forces">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 2]]</ref>

====The Great Hyperspace War====
{{Main|Great Hyperspace War/Legends}}
Sadow's invasion forces gathered together from the far reaches of the Empire, and converged on Khar Shian, from starships to the Massassi ground troops, and finally jumped into hyperspace along the [[Daragon Trail]] towards the Republic.<ref name="FotSE:Forces" /> The Sith forces homed in on the locator aboard ''Starbreaker 12'',<ref name="FotSE:First Encounter">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 3]]</ref> coming out of hyperspace around the unstable red-supergiant star [[Primus Goluud/Legends|Primus Goluud]].<ref name="TEA" /> There, Sadow assigned a mining flotilla and their crews to mine Lignan crystals from Phaegon III for the upcoming battle of [[Kirrek]].<ref name="LTotS:Precipice" /><ref name="Crosscurrent" /> A few months later,<ref name="Crosscurrent" /> he deployed his forces simultaneously to consume the entire Republic,<ref name="FotSE:First Encounter" /> while he held back at Primus Goluud in his meditation sphere. Sadow knew that the Sith did not have the numbers to defeat the Republic navy, so he relied on surprise,<ref name="TEA" /> and also cast Sith illusions through Sith sorcery to make the invasion forces seem larger than they really were.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="FotSE:First Encounter" /> The Sith Empire took the Koros system by surprise, exhausted by the recent [[Unification Wars (Koros)/Legends|Unification Wars]]. With Koros major, Kirrek, and all the other planets under [[Empress Teta/Legends|Empress Teta]] collapsing under the seemingly infinite forces of the Sith, the Sith moved along the Koros trunk line to overwhelm [[Foerost/Legends|Foerost]], then [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], [[Kaikielius/Legends|Kaikielius]], [[Metellos/Legends|Metellos]], [[Basilisk]], and eventually [[Shawken]], where Republic shipyards were stationed.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Battle_of_Coruscant_Great_Hyperspace_War.jpg|thumb|right|400px|Naga Sadow's Sith landing forces of Sith Lords and Massassi warriors overwhelm Coruscant's defenses.]]
The Republic defenders struggled against the unstoppable forces of the Sith, and their unique weapons.<ref name="TEA" /> On Coruscant, the Jedi on the planet had been cautioned of an impending Sith invasion by [[Memit Nadill]] through Jori Daragon<ref name="FotSE:Forces" /> and Jedi Master [[Relin Druur]],<ref name="Crosscurrent" /> but they could not prepare in time for the attack. Lead by Sith Lord [[Shar Dakhan]], the Sith landing forces there forced their way to the steps of [[Senate Hall]], where a last band of Jedi continued to repel the waves of Sith onslaught.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="FotSE:First Encounter" /> However, on Koros Major, Gav Daragon had been made Commander of the armies taking over the planet,<ref name="FotSE:First Encounter" /> but was now betraying the Sith after the death of his friend [[Aarrba]] the Hutt. He flew back to Primus Goluud, and fired on Sadow's meditation sphere, hoping to break the Dark Lord's concentration, and to stop the sorcery he was working over the armies of the Sith. Just as Coruscant was about to fall to the surging Sith forces, Sadow's concentration was broken, and the illusions disappeared, showing the true extent of the Sith armies. The Republic forces there launched a counterstrike with what they had left of their military on the confused Sith, pushing them back into a retreat. On Kirrek, the Sith swarmed and continued to break through the planet's defenses. Even attempts of Battle meditation by Jedi [[Odan-Urr/Legends|Odan-Urr]] failed to have an effect on the single minded Massassi in their rage.<ref name="FotSE:Dogs">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 4]]</ref> But like Coruscant, the Sith push was eventually slowed. The Celegian Jedi Master [[Ooroo/Legends|Ooroo]] released toxic cyanogen gas to poison the Sith in the area, sacrificing his life in the process, but still the Sith continued to push forward. At this stage, the chances of victory for the Sith seemed slim, and when reinforcements from Ronika arrived allied with the Kirrek defenders, their chances diminished even further. The Sith retreated and the Republic allied forces emerged victorious.<ref name="FotSE:Dogs" /><ref name="FotSE:End">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 5|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 5]]</ref>

Republic forces and reinforcements from Anaxes gained confidence with the sudden disappearance of Sith forces, and pushed back the retreating<ref name="FotSE:Dogs" /> Sith armada back to Koros Major.<ref name="TEA" /> Also, Jori Daragon, who was at the death of Aarrba, followed Gav from Koros Major, and called on Empress Teta's fleet for assistance. The Tetan<ref name="FotSE:Dogs" /> and other Republic forces<ref name="TEA" /> emerged from hyperspace at Primus Goluud, to confront Sadow and the remnants of his recalled forces.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="FotSE:Dogs" /> Sadow had previously tricked Gav Daragon and was now on his Sith battleship, while he left Gav trapped on his damaged meditation sphere. The Republic and Sith forces clashed before Sadow caused the red-supergiant star to go supernova, killing Gav Daragon in the process, while he and his remnants jumped back to the Sith Empire.<ref name="FotSE:Dogs" />

In Sith space, Ludo Kressh had survived. He had since gathered his own forces, rallying those Sith Lords who chose to remain behind, as well as promising them wealth and power under him if they allied with him against Sadow. Consequently, with their support, he seized power to become the Dark Lord of the Sith of the Sith Empire, while Sadow was out trying to expand into the Republic.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="DSS" /><ref name="FotSE:End" /> When Sadow arrived back over Korriban to try to drum up more Sith forces, Kressh revealed himself. Sadow was informed that the title of Dark Lord had been stripped of him, and how Kressh used a decoy ship to stage his own death above Khar Delba. Dark Lord Kressh then went on to exile Sadow from Sith space forever.<ref name="FotSE:End" /> The two Sith fleets clashed in a battle of pride,<ref name="TEA" /> with Kressh devastating Sadow's damaged ships.<ref name="DSS" /> However, the battle was ended when Sadow ordered one of his doomed ships to crash into Kressh's flagship, killing the Dark Lord. The remnants of Kressh's armada held back, choosing not to continue fighting Sadow's forces.<ref name="FotSE:End" />

Immediately after, Republic forces who had followed the Daragon Trail to the Sith Empire came out of hyperspace near Sadow's battered fleet. The Republican fleet devastated Sadow's, taking victory against his fleet. After Sadow refused Empress Teta's offer to surrender, he made a barricade with his remaining ships and set course for the [[Denarii Nova|Denarii binary stars]].<ref name="FotSE:End" /> He then used the Force<ref name="TEA" /> and the remaining power he had aboard his ship to [[Battle at the Denarii Nova|cause]] a supernova in each of the stars, escaping and eliminating his Republic pursuers in the process. With Sadow thought dead in the explosions of the stars, Empress Teta recalled the Republic fleet and left the fragmented Empire.<ref name="FotSE:End" />

At this point the Empire posed no threat to the Republic,<ref name="Timeline 12">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 12: The Great Hyperspace War|int=Timeline 12: The Great Hyperspace War}}</ref> however Supreme Chancellor [[Pultimo]]<ref name="TEA" /> was unsatisfied.<ref name="Timeline 12" /> He soon ordered an invasion of Sith space<ref name="TEA" /> to annihilate Sith civilization entirely and ensure the Sith never returned. It was the Republic's and the Jedi's mission to ensure no remnants of the Sith Empire remained.<ref name="Timeline 12" /> In effect, hundreds of Republic warships invaded the Stygian Caldera to take on the disordered Empire&mdash;still in turmoil following the death of their Sith leader Ludo Kressh.<ref name="TEA" /> The Jedi Order also invaded with their [[Jedi Shadow]]s and sought to destroy all they found of the Sith teachings and ways, though some of their ranks denounced this need to destroy.<ref name="KotOR CG" /> The Jedi and the Republic destroyed the Sith Lords, their [[Sith artifact/Legends|artifacts]], [[Sith talisman/Legends|talismans]] and strongholds,<ref name="TotJC" /> eventually driving the Sith to the point of surrender.<ref name="TEA" /> During this period the Jedi Urr would use a unique way to combat the Sith: instead of inflicting harm, he chose to take the power of individual Sith away, stripping Sith of their use of the dark side. He would use this technique so frequently on the Sith that he would become an adept of [[Wall of light|the technique]].<ref name="EotW" /> Shar Dakhan&mdash;now the acting Dark Lord in the absence of Kressh and Sadow&mdash;had his Massassi warriors ram the invading fleets in suicide attacks as a last and only option. The heavy casualties inflicted by the Sith in this manner forced the Republic into a temporary retreat. Eventually though, the Sith were driven to defeat, and many lower-caste Sith killed themselves ritualistically.<ref name="TEA" /> Within a few years, the Empire crumbled<ref name="Heritage of the Sith" /> and the Republic had finally emerged victorious from the war, though at a great cost to their own.<ref name="FotSE:End" />

=====Dissolution=====
The Sith worlds were absorbed into the Republic,<ref name="Heritage of the Sith" /> but the Jedi chose not to destroy all the palaces, strongholds, libraries, and [[Talisman (artifact)|talismans]] of the Sith after the war, selecting a few to keep intact and study should the Sith threaten them again. At the end of the Great Hyperspace War it was widely thought that the Sith in both religion and species were extinct,<ref name="TotJC" /> and many compared the attitude the Jedi had against the existence of the Sith to that of [[Bothan/Legends|Bothans]] in an [[Ar'krai]].<ref name="END:TSD" /> In reality, most of those Sith that were not killed in bloody war<ref name="TotJC" /> were chased far into [[Unknown Regions/Legends|deep space]] where none had returned from.<ref name="Daniel Erickson Clarification" /> However, despite the thoroughness of the onslaught by the Jedi and the Republic, the Sith species<ref name="KotOR CG" /><ref name="JATM" /> and their culture continued to persist.<ref name="TotJC" />

Some Sith forces that survived the Great Hyperspace War fled Jedi Shadows and [[Jedi Sentinel/Legends|sentinels]] to the unknown regions of the galaxy to recover and plan revenge on the Jedi and the Republic in secret. Explorers in these regions were likely to come across Sith settlements during these times and throughout the [[Old Republic era]]. During other eras however, chances of this happening became less likely.<ref name="TUR" />

Some Sith of a predominantly Human stock crew aboard the ship ''[[Omen]]'', under the command of Sadow also managed to survive the war. The ship had been knocked off course in hyperspace from a collision with their sister ship [[Harbinger (Hammerhead-class)|''Harbinger'']], due to an attack by a Jedi starfighter while mining for [[Lignan]] ore before the battle of Kirrek.<ref name="LTotS:Precipice" /> These Sith found their way to a previously unknown planet called [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]] by the natives. The survivors of Human and some Sith descent subjected the natives, coming to be worshiped as the god-like [[Skyborn]] of the native [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] legend.<ref name="LTotS:Skyborn" />

Some other Sith also fled to [[Vjun/Legends|Vjun]] after the war. A small number of Sith<ref name="TEA" /> and Sith supporters fled to [[Thule/Legends|Thule]]&mdash;a planet that had previously been inhabited by Sith stealth forces&mdash;to regroup with Sith special forces. Believing their defeat at the hands of the Jedi and the Republic was only temporary, the Sith there on Thule strove to build up an advance force, lead in a military fashion to take revenge against their enemies.<ref name="GatORW">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> These were not the only Sith to escape however, Sadow had also managed to escape the annihilation he had caused at the Denarii nova. Exiled from Sith space by the previously reigning Dark Lord Kressh,<ref name="FotSE:End" /><ref name="Masters and Students of the Force">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 1|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 1]]</ref> and declared as a criminal by the Republic, he and his followers aboard [[Corsair (Derriphan-class)|his lone ship]] found their way to the [[Yavin system/Legends|Yavin system]]. There they settled on the jungle moon of [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], where Sadow planned to build a base, and expand from there.<ref name="FotSE:End" />

Elsewhere, on [[Tund/Legends|Tund]], the pure-blooded Sith sorcerers that had survived there over the millennia had escaped the devastation that had spread across many other worlds from the Great Hyperspace War, alongside Sith&ndash;Human Hybrids that had settled there after the Dark Jedi exiles conquered the Sith. Eventually the pure-blooded Sith society there evolved into what would be known as the [[Sorcerers of Tund/Legends|Sorcerers of Tund]]. These dark side Force-users<ref name="TEA" /> investigated heavily into the use of the Force, enough to drive some members mad. They were capable of producing powerful and extreme powers in thaumaturgy, transmogrification, and phantasm.<ref name="KotOR CG" />

Another Sith refuge<ref name="TEA" /> and focal point for escaping Sith included the world of [[Ambria/Legends|Ambria]].<ref name="TotJC" /> A Sith sorceress had enslaved the native population there, and forced them to construct a giant, black obelisk over a century. Once it was completed, she experimented by performing an ancient Sith ritual using Sith sorcery. However, the sorcery proved beyond her own abilities and resulted in a release of dark side energy that enveloped the planet, transforming it into a desolate desert-world, and destroying herself and the native species in the process.<ref name="DB:PoD">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref><ref name="DB:DoE">''[[Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil]]''</ref> Centuries before 4,000 BBY, the spirits of the Sith that had fled there and died remained, embedded in the planet itself, before eventually being trapped in [[Lake]] [[Lake Natth|Natth]] by the Jedi [[Thon]].<ref name="TotJC" />

Following their defeat of the Great Hyperspace War and the carnage on Korriban, a small armada carrying at least a few hundred Sith<ref name="Gnost">''[[The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural]]''</ref><ref name="Timeline 11">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 11: Rebirth of the Sith Empire|int=Timeline 11: Rebirth of the Sith Empire}}</ref> fled in the direction of the unknown regions,<ref name="TEA" /> using random hyperspace co-ordinates in desperation to escape the Jedi and the Republic.<ref name="SWTOR:Dromund Kaas">{{Holonet|planets|dromund-kaas|Dromund Kaas}}</ref> In their retreat, the Sith also brought with them tens of thousands<ref name="Gnost" /> of prisoners from their early victories against the Republic, whose lives and descendants would be condemned to slavery.<ref name="Revan" /> Deep in unknown space, this handful of Sith forces forged a [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|new Sith Empire]], led by the newly proclaimed [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]] and his [[Dark Council|most trusted Sith Lords]].<ref name="SWTOR:Sith Empire">{{Holonet|allegiances|sith-empire|The Sith Empire}}</ref> For twenty years the Sith armada drifted through deep space after the Great Hyperspace War, utilizing random hyperspace jumps and blind scouting missions to lead their way.<ref name="SWTOR:Dromund Kaas" /> Late in this process, the wandering Sith came across the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] [[Chiss Ascendancy/Legends|Ascendancy]], and like all other instances where the Sith came across civilizations with resources and technology that the Sith deemed useful, the renewed Empire demanded that the Chiss surrender to the rule of the Emperor, or be conquered, enslaved, and/or destroyed entirely in the case of refusal. The Chiss surprised the Sith in their response, however, seeking non-forceful means to solve the conflict. The Chiss ruling class requested a meeting with the Sith, which the Sith military leadership agreed to in their confusion. In private, the best Chiss negotiators met with important Imperial diplomats, including the commander of the Imperial Guard, eventually concluding that the Chiss would become the first official allies of the Empire.<ref name="Chiss">{{HolonetOld|inhabitants|chiss|Chiss}}</ref> Eventually however, twenty years after their escape, the Empire stumbled and settled upon the long-forgotten Sith world of [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]].<ref name="SWTOR:Dromund Kaas" /> Here the Emperor would further manipulate his followers to his plans of conquest of the Republic, by re-christening this planet as the "true" homeworld of the original Sith species.<ref name="Revan" /><ref name="DrewDromund" /> Similarly, ancient artifacts, tomes and manuscripts were available, at least one claiming Dark Jedi exiles arrived on the claimed Sith homeworld around 14,000 BBY.<ref name="Revan" />

Meanwhile, fifteen years after landing on Kesh, the Red Sith portion of the Lost Tribe of Sith secretly used [[cyanogen silicate]] to kill off all the people in a Keshiri village. Trying to portray it as a plague that could potentially threaten the Human Sith there, it was a last attempt to try and convince the Lost Tribe to focus on getting off world. However, one of the Human Sith who had suffered under the care of Dark Lord Kressh had a grudge against all Red Sith as a result. [[Seelah Korsin|She]] had secretly been killing all the Red Sith offspring born over their time on Kesh, and once she realized what the Red Sith were doing under the leadership of a Sith named [[Ravilan Wroth]], she framed them. Eventually she converted her [[Yaru Korsin|husband]], the [[Grand Lord]] to her cause, and launched a specicide event against the Red Sith there, killing all the Red Sith on the isolated planet.<ref name="LTotS:Paragon" />

Sadow never succeeded in expanding from the fourth moon of Yavin. With the intention of creating guardians to watch over his legacy, Sadow eventually used [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]] to commit heinous experiments on the Massassi he had brought on his ship, transforming them into more powerful and violent, but less intelligent mutants.<ref name="Death of a Dark Jedi">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 4]]</ref><ref name="Timeline 7">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 7: Peace for the Republic?|int=Timeline 7: Peace for the Republic?}}</ref> Eventually, Sadow put himself in suspended animation,<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> never forgetting the Empire he had once ruled.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> Over the centuries, these primitive, hunched, monstrous Massassi savages would come to worship one of Sadow's [[Sith wyrm|alchemical creations]] as a god,<ref name="KotOR CG" /> and fulfilled their role as guardians of Sadow's legacy.<ref name="Death of a Dark Jedi" /> This included defending Sadow's temples against Dark Jedi [[Freedon Nadd]] around [[4400 BBY]]. Nadd awakened Sadow, and became Sadow's apprentice. After learning all he could from Sadow and his knowledge stores, Nadd killed Sadow,<ref name="NEC" /> and with the holocrons of both [[Darth Andeddu]]<ref name="CSWE" /> and King Adas, he went on to found a Sith Order not directly associated with the Sith species.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" />

[[4000 BBY/Legends|One thousand years]] after the fall of the Sith Empire, dark side devotees had begun to discover these Sith caches on remote worlds, where those that did not perish in the Great Hyperspace War sought to preserve their knowledge for future generations. Housing ancient Sith lore, talismans and the like, these dark side retreats and library-temples were of great concern to the Jedi Order. However these sanctuaries continued to elude the sight of the Jedi.<ref name="TotJC" />

====The Great Sith War====
{{Main|Great Sith War/Legends}}
Yavin IV and its mutant Massassi inhabitants would be visited again centuries later by a student of the spirit of Nadd&mdash;[[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]], in his ambitions to obtain Sith secrets. Initially, the primitive, tribal Massassi defended the temples<ref name="Death of a Dark Jedi" /> their ancestors had built in Sadow's honor<ref name="KotOR CG" /> and attacked Kun. They stripped his ship and captured the intruder, bringing him to the [[Temple of Fire]] to be devoured in a "Massassi blood sacrifice" ritual.
